notes: Provider catalogue initialization and refresh reject more than 1024 entries, duplicate exact IDs, invalid display names, zero published limits and output limits exceeding published context. models.list accepts explicit nativeCatalogPage through actual Gateway and administrator routes. Legacy/default Gateway dispatch and the existing administrator ID list are retained. Unknown context/output limits remain null. advertisedCapabilities come from SDK descriptors and may be adapter/provider defaults; source=provider_sdk_catalogue and liveCapabilitiesVerified=false avoid claiming per-account verification

Nine actual CLI/WebSocket scenarios include full page, continuation, unavailable, digest mismatch, duplicate, unsupported capability, bad numeric limit, extra credential field and absent selected model. One RPC per invocation, no implicit refresh or inference

CLI gateway refresh-models explicitly requests read/write and the previously observed SHA. Gateway requires write/admin in addition to the base read method authorization, and rejects mixed operations. One catalogue refresh can be in flight; ten-second total wait and drop/cancel/shutdown guards bound uncooperative model-list futures

Refresh invokes list_models once and never completes/streams/embeds or changes the configured model. Before cache publication it revalidates descriptors, the actual adapter identity, configuration generation, pinned/default selection and cancellation. Old cache survives failure, removed selection, concurrent switch or timeout

Eight controlled refresh lifecycle cases cover success, caller cancellation, dropped future, missing default model, concurrent configuration change, provider replacement, shutdown and actual ten-second timeout. Simultaneous second refresh performs no list request; original provider generation and selection remain unchanged except the deliberate replacement/shutdown test actions

Five real CLI refresh scenarios verify scopes, pinned request, refusal and invalid inference/selection/extra-field receipts, with no second RPC or replay. Six actual daemon provider/source runs validate shared page/receipt schemas, one extra model-list call for explicit refresh and zero extra inference; a separate paired read-only device can list but cannot refresh

Full single pages independently verify the digest. Individual continuation pages only pin the complete snapshot and do not cryptographically prove omitted models. No alias resolution, account verification, pricing or graphical selection workflow is claimed

The preceding configuration ledger describes an earlier validated local snapshot. Files subsequently extended for catalogue work have current hashes here; earlier ledger bytes are not rewritten. M3-06.01 acceptance remains the narrow typed-config scope, while M3-07 remains open

No external downloads/version upgrades, real provider/cloud accounts, paid generation, production proxy/server changes, migration, deployment, release or mobile hardware were used. Earlier accounting edits were retained. All owned commands completed synchronously; no branch, commit or push was performed
recovery: Read the first cached page again after a digest mismatch or successful refresh; never generate a completion merely to rebuild a catalogue
A refused/failed refresh retains the old cache and selected model. Review the error and current snapshot before an explicit retry; no automatic refresh or fallback model is used

Unavailable or disabled provider state must be resolved through the appropriate explicit configuration/authentication workflow; a catalogue page is not proof of readiness, capability or bill settlement

notes: This follow-up is the latest catalogue wire shape in this unpublished increment. Pages carry providerGeneration; refresh receipts also carry requestedSha256. CLI cases now cover ten page scenarios and seven refresh scenarios, including zero generation and a valid receipt for the wrong request digest. Complete page hashes and actual six-dialect/source daemon responses pass the shared validator

Prior top-level source/artifact hashes are historical snapshots, not hashes of later builds. Latest changed-source witnesses and final checks are in this follow-up. No original accounting v1 digest or sealed compatibility contract was changed

Provider generations remain process-local, not cross-restart durable identities. Reconnect requires rereading the current catalogue. Wall-clock observation timestamps do not establish monotonic freshness or real capability proof; these limits remain open

ModelCatalogueRequest binds worker connection and monotonic UI request sequence with one pending request. Worker validates through claw-protocol before emitting a result. Late or mismatched events are ignored, failure preserves the old page, and successful refresh invalidates the old cursor until an explicit cache read

Six real WebSocket worker scenarios cover pages, refresh, refused refresh, malformed page, unavailable provider and previous connection refusal. Exact RPC counts and a refused local chat ACK prove catalogue results are not chat results

Rendering tests cover widths20/40/80/120 and heights10/24, long wide-character labels, active tab visibility and unknown limits. First test mistakenly searched a wrapped multi-line label as a single line; corrected the assertion to reconstruct ordered display content without weakening layout checks
